Consult Summary:
- 65-year-old female with 5 days of dry cough and continuous green nasal discharge, subjective fevers and myalgia; clinical impression by doctor: probable viral chest/sinus infection.
- Advised symptomatic care, obtain thermometer, monitor for red flags (persistent fever, worsening cough, sputum, haemoptysis, chest pain, or shortness of breath); diabetes increases risk of bacterial infection and may prompt antibiotics if deteriorates.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Acute cough and rhinorrhea (suspected viral chest/sinus infection)
- Timeline and symptoms: onset ~5 days ago; dry cough occurring ~every 20–30 minutes; no sputum production; continuous nasal discharge described as "pretty green".
- Associated symptoms: subjective feeling hot and intermittent chills, myalgia, transient diarrhea at onset (resolved), no vomiting, no current diarrhea.
- Systems review / pertinent negatives: no chest pain, no shortness of breath, no haemoptysis, no sore throat reported, no headache or vision change, no rash.
- Social/other relevant: able to eat/drink and pass urine normally; height 5'5", weight 65 kg.
- Examination / objective findings: none recorded; temperature not measured.
- Clinical impression / differential: clinician considers likely viral chest/sinus infection; bacterial infection possible given diabetes.
- Management given: advised to obtain thermometer and check temperature; continue symptomatic measures (Lemsip/lozenges) but avoid additional paracetamol-containing products while taking Lemsip; cough suppressant only if unable to sleep; seek review if temperature persistent >37.5–38°C, ongoing fever, worsening cough, development of productive sputum, haemoptysis, chest pain, or shortness of breath. Antibiotics may be considered if symptoms worsen or fever persists.

Issue 2: Type 2 diabetes mellitus
- History: patient states she is diabetic; recent blood test approx. 3 weeks ago reported as "normal."
- Medications: reports taking metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Monitoring / management: not checking blood sugars at home currently; clinician advised to continue regular diabetes follow-up/checks as arranged by GP.
- Relevance: clinician noted diabetes increases risk of bacterial infection.

Issue 3: Hypertension
- History: patient reports hypertension.
- Medications: reports taking lisinopril (name provided; dose/route/frequency not documented; patient later stated "two hundred" when asked dose — conflict noted).
- Monitoring / management: last blood pressure check not recalled by patient; advised to maintain regular BP checks with GP.

Medications:
- Metformin — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Lisinopril — dose/route/frequency not documented (patient mentioned "two hundred" when asked dose; conflict noted).
- Lemsip / lemon lozenges (OTC) — dose/route/frequency not documented (patient reports taking ~2–3/day).
- Unspecified cough syrup — dose/route/frequency not documented (advised for nocturnal use only if required).

Allergies:
- Seasonal hay fever reported (seasonal allergic rhinitis).
- No drug allergies reported.

Past Medical History:
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- Hypertension.

Social History:
- Lives with partner and dog.
- Occupation: office manager.
- Alcohol: reports occasional alcohol ("the odd cherry") — patient-reported phrasing; frequency not quantified.
- Smoking: not documented / patient did not respond to smoking question.

Preventative History:
- Recent blood test for diabetes ~3 weeks ago reported as normal.
- No information provided regarding cervical screening, mammogram, PSA, fecal occult blood test, bone mineral density, vaccinations, optometry, or skin checks.

Physical Examination:
- Vital signs: none measured or reported in transcript (temperature not checked).
- Exam findings: none documented; nasal discharge described by patient as green; otherwise no objective exam recorded.

Plan:
- Patient to obtain a thermometer and monitor temperature.
- Continue symptomatic treatment (Lemsip/lozenges); avoid additional paracetamol-containing medications while using Lemsip.
- Use cough syrup only at night if cough prevents sleep.
- Monitor for red flags and re-contact clinician/GP if: persistent or recurrent fever >37.5–38°C, worsening cough, development of purulent sputum, haemoptysis, new chest pain, or shortness of breath.
- Consider antibiotics if symptoms worsen or if persistent fever / signs of bacterial infection develop (as per clinician review).
- Continue routine diabetes and hypertension follow-up with GP; resume or maintain home glucose/BP monitoring as advised by GP.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: measured vital signs (temperature, pulse, respiratory rate, blood pressure), focused respiratory examination, smoking status not documented, medication doses/administration details absent for metformin and lisinopril, no objective blood glucose value provided.
- Internal conflicts from transcript: patient stated lisinopril as medication but gave an implausible dose "two hundred" when asked — conflict noted and dose not recorded.
- Transcript quality: overall adequate for clinical content; occasional short pauses/mumbled or truncated responses (address and some single-word answers) but sufficient to extract key history.
